This study investigated the occurrence of the S-cysteine and S-glutathione conjugates of 3MBT (Cys-3MBT and GSH-3MBT) in CBD- and THC- dominant cannabis flowers and proposed them as possible precursor of the odor-thiol 3MBT. Both conjugates were identified for the first time in Cannabis sativa in CBD and THC cultivars by HPLC-QTOF-MS/MS and confirmed with reference standards. In vitro release experiments showed that GSH-3MBT generated 3MBT under moderate thermal conditions, whereas both conjugates released substantial amounts of 3MBT during fermentation with S.cerevisiae. Cys-3MBT and GSH-3MBT were quantified by HPLC-MS/MS at two stages of flower maturation in both cultivars, showing a decrease in their quantity during maturation. The THC-cultivar sample contained higher levels of both precursors at the earliest stage of maturation (Cys-3MBT: 13.01± 0.061 mg/kg ; GSH-3MBT 10.98 ± 0.14 mg/kg) than the CBD-cultivar (Cys-3MBT: 0.85 ± 0.057 mg/kg ; GSH-3MBT 2.96 ± 0.044 mg/kg) sample. Higher levels of the precursors in the THC-cultivar were also correlated with higher levels of free 3MBT (1.79 ± 0.19 mg/kg in THC and 0.075 mg/kg in CBD). These findings identify Cys-3MBT and GSH-3MBT as potential precursors of 3MBT and provide the basis for elucidating the biochemical origin and evolution of this odor-active thiol during Cannabis sativa maturation.

item.title: Dataset of magnetic properties, structure and synthesis of doped barium and strontium M-type hexaferrites
item.description: M-type barium and strontium hexaferrites are the most widely produced permanent-magnet materials, and their structural and magnetic properties are commonly tuned by cationic substitution. The experimental data on doped hexaferrites are dispersed over hundreds of articles and reported with heterogeneous notation, units and descriptors. Here we present HexaMagDB, a manually curated dataset of 4388 records extracted from 662 peer-reviewed articles on doped Ba-and Sr-based M-type hexaferrites. Each record corresponds to one experimentally characterized sample and contains the chemical formula, the dopant elements, their amounts and substituted sites, the synthesis method and procedure, the calcination and sintering conditions, the lattice parameters, crystallite and particle sizes, phase purity and secondary phases, and the saturation and remanent magnetizations, coercivity, squareness ratio, Curie temperature and magnetocrystalline anisotropy field and constant, together with the measurement temperature and maximum applied field. The dataset covers 48 dopant elements in 251 combinations. An interactive online tool for visualization and navigation through the data has also been developed. This dataset can serve as a comprehensive benchmark for predicting the magnetic properties of doped hexaferrites.

item.title: 18O-Informed Metabolomics Reveals Microbial Phosphoryl-Transfer Dynamics and Stress-Induced Changes
item.description: Microbial metabolism provides critical ecosystem functions, yet characterizing microbial metabolic activity in environmental systems remain challenging. Since phosphoryl-transfer reactions are central to energy metabolism, biosynthesis, and metabolic regulation, they have been proposed as a proxy for overall metabolic activity. Some phosphoryl-transfer reactions are known to contribute to the oxygen isotope fractionation between phosphate and water, leaving an isotopic signature of metabolic activity. Although these reactions are well characterized at the level of individual enzymes, their dynamics within the phosphoryl-transfer network remain difficult to resolve, limiting their use for assessing metabolic activity in the environment. Here, we present an 18O stable isotope labeling-based metabolomics workflow to trace phosphoryl-transfer reactions in Escherichia coli. Cells are grown in labeled medium containing ∼10 atom% H218O under optimal and heat-stressed conditions, and 18O incorporation into ATP and other phosphate-containing metabolites is quantified from isotopologue distributions. ATP is labeled within one minute of label introduction and approaches the enrichment of intracellular water in stationary phase, indicating ATP turnover as the main entry point of 18O into the phosphoryl-transfer network. The label rapidly propagates to other nucleotides, sugar phosphates, redox cofactors, and all other measured phosphate-containing metabolites within three hours of label introduction. Normalizing metabolite enrichment to ATP enrichment reveals phosphoryl group turnover that changes with growth phase, indicating net phosphoryl flux through gluconeogenesis into the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) during exponential growth. Heat stress induces moderate effects on growth and central carbon metabolism, but transiently accelerates label accumulation in the non-oxidative PPP and the turnover of NAD+ and NADP+. These results show that 18O-informed metabolomics provides a systematic view of phosphoryl-transfer dynamics and reveals microbial metabolic adaptation under stress, with implications for tracking microbial stress responses and phosphorus cycling in changing environments.

item.title: Functional characterization of a hyperthermophilic glycyl radical enzyme reveals a reductive glycerol pathway in archaea
item.description: The function of the glycyl radical enzyme (GRE) PFL2 from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Archaeoglobus fulgidus has remained unresolved since its discovery. Structural and sequence analyses initially suggested that PFL2 was a B12-independent glycerol dehydratase (GDHt), whereas subsequent structural and transcriptional evidence implicated it as a methylalkylsuccinate synthase involved in anaerobic alkane activation. Difficulties in reconstituting active PFL2 in vitro prevented either assignment from being established biochemically. Here, genome mining identified soluble activating enzymes that enabled us to demonstrate that PFL2 catalyzes glycerol dehydration to 3-hydroxypropionaldehyde (3-HPA). This reaction initiates the reductive glycerol pathway, in which 3-HPA is subsequently reduced to 1,3-propanediol (1,3-PD), an industrially important precursor to polymers and other materials. Although characterized in bacteria, this pathway has not previously been experimentally established in archaea. Motivated by this knowledge gap, we identified three oxidoreductases encoded in the A. fulgidus genome that catalyze the reduction of 3-HPA to 1,3-PD in vitro. Microscale thermophoresis revealed nanomolar-affinity binding between PFL2 and one of these oxidoreductases, AF0339 (apparent Kd = 70–90 nM), and AlphaFold-Multimer modeling predicted a continuous tunnel connecting their active sites, suggesting a possible route for intermediate transfer. Notably, PFL2 and AF0339 exhibited melting temperatures of 80.5 and 85.2 °C, respectively, revealing a thermally stable pair of enzymes catalyzing both steps of the pathway. Together, these findings establish PFL2 as an archaeal GDHt and provide experimental support for a reductive glycerol pathway in archaea. The thermostability of these enzymes further highlights their potential utility in biocatalytic 1,3-PD production.

item.title: A linear-scaling explicitly correlated local natural orbital CCSD(T) approach
item.description: We introduce an integral-direct, linear-scaling, local explicitly correlated (F12) coupled-cluster (CC) singles, doubles, and perturbative triples [CCSD(T)] approach building on our established local natural orbital (LNO) CCSD(T) [J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2018, 14, 4193] and local second-order Møller–Plesset F12 [J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2026, 22, 2946] techniques. By generating and transforming all the required integrals on-the-fly, the algorithm eliminates integral storage requirements, resulting in asymptotically constant memory usage and negligible disk I/O. A key strength of the implementation is the application of the CCSD(F12*) ansatz alongside our (T+) triples correction—currently the most comprehensive scheme incorporating F12 approximations — which delivers rapid basis set convergence. Benchmark tests show that, under default truncation settings, the method recovers over 99.9% of the canonical explicitly correlated CCSD(T) correlation energy, achieving reaction energy errors under 1 kJ/mol. Compared to the complete basis set limit of CCSD(T), the average deviation of reaction energies remains around 1 kJ/mol. Overall, our results demonstrate that combining LNO-CCSD(T) with explicit correlation provides an efficient strategy for high-accuracy calculations on large molecular systems using modest basis sets.

item.title: Pressure-Induced Formation of Intermetallic CrBi2
item.description: Binary transition-metal bismuth compounds offer a new class of solid-state materials with emergent properties such as magnetism, superconductivity, thermoelectricity and nontrivial topology. Under ambient conditions, Bi shows immiscibility with many other elements. High-pressure can offers an alternative thermodynamic landscape for Bi-based intermetallic systems. Herein, we computationally explore the energy landscape for the immiscible Cr-Bi systems under high-pressure. At 60 GPa, CrBi2 having a CuAl2-type structure with -Cr-Cr-Cr- chains and Bi2 dimers is found to be thermodynamically stable with respect to the elemental solids. The structure is dynamically stable and exhibits ferromagnetic character. Furthermore, electronic structure calculation reveals notable Cr-Cr and Bi-Bi bonding interaction, along with distinctive Cr 3d and Bi 6p bonding interaction. Apart from homoatomic interactions, Cr 3d and Bi 6p hybridization plays a critical role in stabilizing CrBi2 under pressure. This finding provides a viable route towards discovery of new binary intermetallic compounds and extend the compositional space for chemical synthesis at high-pressure.

item.title: Coupling kinetic and techno-economic models reveals hidden biodesign targets
item.description: Metabolic and bioprocess engineering aim to achieve high fermentation titer, rate and yield (TRY), yet no general framework connects these interdependent metrics to facility-scale economics. We introduce NSKinetics, an agile computational framework embedding biochemically structured kinetic models within facility-scale process simulation, techno-economic analysis, uncertainty analysis, global sensitivity analysis, and optimization. We find that for yeast-based ethanol and isobutanol production in a corn biorefinery, cost uncertainty for today's technology is governed by scale, feedstock price, and co-product value rather than ethanol fermentation kinetics. Nonintuitively, while eliminating ethanol inhibition enables a 3.7-fold increase in ethanol productivity, it makes the facility unprofitable by diverting too much carbon to cell growth. Across eight Bayesian optimization campaigns over 12 enzyme-expression, tolerance, and substrate-feeding decisions, TRY-optimized strains were poorly profitable, and a profitability-only campaign stalled at an ethanol-only optimum (15.8% internal rate of return, IRR). However, combining the approaches with a profitability campaign informed by the TRY campaigns' exploration revealed the potential to engineer an ethanol-isobutanol co-producing strain with 27.3% IRR. Fermentation metrics are therefore insufficient proxies for profitability, but valuable guides across the rugged profitability landscape.

item.title: Squaramide-based ultrasensitive and reversible colourimetric dual sensor for the detection of copper and metal-ion-assisted acetate anion
item.description: A tripodal squaramide–quinoline– tris(2-aminoethyl)amine (TREN) chemosensor, TSQAQ, was synthesised in good yield using diethylsquarate, 8-aminoquinoline and tris(2aminoethyl)amine as starting materials. The chemosensor was evaluated as a dual-mode colorimetric platform for the selective naked-eye detection of Cu2+ in DMSO and Cd2+ (precursor was cadmium acetate, CA) in acetonitrile. TSQAQ exhibited sensitivity towards Cu2+ via the ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) mechanism, producing an absorption peak at 450 nm and a distinctive colour change from colourless to bright yellow, irrespective of the Cu2+ counteranion screened. In contrast, the addition of CA yields an absorption peak at 420 nm and a colour transformation from colourless to pale yellow, with confirms the cooperative binding of Cd2+ by the squaramide moiety through hydrogen bonding. The limits of detection (LODs) were determined to be 97 nM (Cu2+) and 3 nM (Cd2+). Binding constants of 2.51 × 104 M-1 and 1.97 × 104 M-1 were determined using the Benesi-Hildebrand equation. The binding stoichiometry of TSQAQ with Cd2+ was established as 1:1 using the Job plot method. FTIR and 1H NMR titration studies indicated the involvement of TREN nitrogen, quinoline imine nitrogen, and squaramide carbonyl oxygen atoms in metal-ion coordination. Cu2+ sensing was reversible upon the addition of EDTA, with 94% signal recovery maintained over five cycles, enabling the implementation of an INHIBIT molecular logic gate. For practical applications, TSQAQ-coated paper strips were employed for the naked-eye detection of Cu2+ ions in real environmental water samples, including river water, seawater, and tap water.

item.title: Constant-pH Molecular Dynamics Rationalizes Photoinduced Decarboxylation in Fluorescent Proteins
item.description: Many advanced imaging techniques, such as super-resolution microscopy, rely on photoinduced transformations of fluorescent proteins. In photoinduced decarboxylation, light absorption triggers loss of CO2 from an acidic residue near the chromophore, often accompanied by a change in chromophore protonation that switches the protein to a fluorescent form, as in PA-GFP. Evidence from proteins in which this reaction has been observed indicates that the decarboxylating residue must be present in its deprotonated form. Because protonation states are difficult to determine experimentally, here we perform constant-pH molecular dynamics (CpHMD) simulations on a set of fluorescent protein variants, and find that the predicted protonation states are consistent with the observed photoinduced properties. This includes superfolder GFP, which does not decarboxylate, and its T203D mutant, in which two residues undergo decarboxylation. CpHMD therefore offers a practical route to predicting which variants are capable of photoinduced decarboxylation and to designing new photoactivatable proteins.

item.title: Radial Kernel Attention for Long-Range Modeling in Polymer Machine Learning Force Fields
item.description: We introduce Radial Kernel Attention (RKA) for long-range modeling in polymer machine learning force fields. Local neighbor graphs constrain communication across polymer chains and their surrounding environments, while explicit all-pair attention incurs quadratic cost. RKA maps atomic distances from the cluster centroid to learned radial features and combines their overlap with content-dependent queries and keys. Factorized aggregation and readout enable global feature exchange at linear cost in atom count for fixed feature dimensions. We insert the invariant scalar update between EquiformerV3 local blocks and obtain conservative forces by differentiating the total energy, including its radial coordinate dependence. We evaluate energy and force prediction for finite polymer-derived clusters in OPoly26. Our models are trained on the official training split for 12 epochs and evaluated directly after training on the complete official validation split. A matched 5M comparison shows that RKA reduces per-atom energy and force MAEs by 67.4% and 36.3%, respectively. The 20M RKA model is compared with UMA-S-1.2 and UMA-S-1.2.1 on the same validation structures. The 20M model attains a total-energy MAE of 15.81 meV and a force MAE of 2.619 meV/Å; its per-atom energy MAE is 0.1182 meV/atom. RKA provides a compact global communication pathway that improves energy and force prediction on the evaluated polymer-derived clusters.

item.title: Synthesis and Engineering of Bio-Based Porous Organic Polymers for Gold Recovery
item.description: The development of functional porous materials from renewable resources offers a promising strategy to reduce reliance on fossil-derived feedstocks and advance sustainable materials technologies. Here, we report the facile synthesis of bio-based porous organic polymers (bioPOPs) through the polycondensation of vanillin-derived organic dialdehydes and inexpensive diamine monomers. The synthetic approach demonstrates good generality, enabling vanillin-derived monomers bearing different functional substituents (H, OH, CH3, OCH3, and NO2) to be converted into bioPOPs with high specific surface areas of up to 523 m2/g and abundant microporosity. Furthermore, cellulose nanofibers (CNF) were employed as templates for the in situ interfacial polymerization of bioPOPs on their surfaces, allowing the resulting hybrid nanofibers to be processed into freestanding composite films. Benefiting from their rich microporosity and abundant nitrogen-containing functional groups, both pristine bioPOPs and CNF@bioPOP composite films exhibited efficient [AuCl4]- capture from aqueous solutions, with adsorption capacities of up to 1093 mg/g, rapid adsorption kinetics, and excellent selectivity over competing metal ions. More importantly, the materials demonstrated highly efficient and selective gold recovery from real electronic waste leachate, highlighting their potential for preciousmetal recovery from secondary resources. The freestanding composite films further offer advantages for practical separation applications through their processability and potential integration into continuous flow systems. Overall, this work demonstrates the transformation of renewable resources into functional porous materials for precious-metal recovery from secondary waste streams, establishing a fully sustainable and circular approach to resource utilization.

item.title: The Importance of Base and Solvent in the Ni-Mediated Decarboxylation of Pentafluorobenzoic Acid
item.description: An experimental kinetic study of the decarboxylation of pentafluorobenzoic acid is reported. This work demonstrates a thermal decarboxylation pathway that is operative under conditions commonly employed for catalytic decarboxylative coupling reactions. This work also reveals a dramatic rate enhancement for the benzoate salt relative to the neutral acid and the importance of basic additives in accelerating the decarboxylation of the pentafluorobenzoic acid. Additionally, decarboxylation of the acid displays a strong solvent dependence with the polar aprotic solvent DMA leading to more rapid thermal decarboxylation as well as an increased influence of Ni additives.

item.title: Redox-active ligand facilitates HNO generation in a super-reduced dinitrosyl iron complex
item.description: Dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) are widespread biological nitric oxide (NO) storage and delivery motifs, yet their highly delocalized electronic structure generally resists NO-centered reductive chemistry. Here, we establish ligandcentered reduction as a strategy for unlocking nitroxyl (HNO)-generating DNIC reactivity. A redox-active formazanate ligand (L) stabilizes a super-reduced formal {LFe(NO)2}11 state beyond the conventional {Fe(NO)2}9/10 redox pair. EPR and Mössbauer spectroscopy, together with density functional theory calculations, identify predominantly ligand-centered reduction, yielding an {Fe(NO)2}10 unit coupled to a formazanate radical dianion, L2−•. Electronic communication between the reduced ligand and the [Fe(NO)2] unit enhances Fe-to-NO π backbonding, consistent with experimental ν(NO) redshifts. Importantly, protonation triggers HNO release, representing an unprecedented example of HNO generation from the super reduced DNIC scaffold. Isotopically distinct H14NO/H15NO is trapped with PPh3, along with the 14/15N2O characterization. Calculations support direct nitrosyl protonation to form an Fe-bound HNO intermediate, followed by solvent-assisted HNO release and subsequent N2O formation. These findings establish that ligand-centered electron accommodation coupled to nitrosyl protonation enables HNO generation from a formally super-reduced DNIC, extending DNIC reactivity beyond conventional NO donation.

item.title: Air pollution sensing to urban air quality insight: review of spatially interpolated data products from sensor networks
item.description: Air pollution adversely impacts health globally, disproportionately affecting urban populations. Regulatory monitoring is often too spatially coarse to capture true intra-urban variability, needed to prioritize and guide localized interventions and policies. High-density lower-cost sensor (LCS) networks, mobile monitoring, satellite-derived products, and advanced interpolation techniques are emerging to support higher spatial resolution characterization. However, results from related studies are varied, disconnected across different fields, and as yet with no defined standards or guidance. This review examines the literature from 2005-2025 to systematically compare data collection and modeling pipelines for accuracy and application to the intra-urban challenge. 166 studies from regional to neighborhood scale were analyzed quantitatively on monitoring network characteristics (geographic location, spatial density, target pollutants, study duration) and interpolation modeling approaches (algorithms, predictive covariates, performance metrics). Studies from Europe, Asia, and North America dominated the literature, with particulate matter being the most studied pollutant. While 95% of studies had measurement density below 20,000 km2/device (metro scale), none had sufficient resolution for capturing intra-urban heterogeneity. Modeling approaches shifted over time from primarily geostatistical methods toward increasingly sophisticated machine learning and deep learning techniques incorporating diverse covariates, including meteorology, land use, traffic patterns, and satellite data products. More than measurement density or model complexity, strategic use of both static and dynamic covariates in data driven models was most consistently associated with performance improvement for interpolation of both PM2.5 and NOx. However, major gaps remain including (1) imbalance in data availability geographically, temporally, and across pollutant species, leading to major challenges in assessing and achieving transferability of models globally, (2) limited data availability at appropriate intra-urban scale for most metro areas, (3) lack of evaluation and reporting standards necessary to truly compare performance of different data-model pipelines, and (4) general lack of generating or reporting uncertainty quantification on model outputs, critically needed for interpretability and sensitivity analyses. These gaps point to an urgent need for not only interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation but also discipline-wide guidance that will enable objective assessment of model performance and state-of-the-art, including shared benchmark datasets, standardized evaluation metrics, mandatory unit reporting, and guidelines for complete model specifications.

item.title: Ensemble of ∆-ML Models for Quantum Chemistry Level of Theory Selection for Interaction Energies
item.description: Ab initio quantum chemical approaches for computing interactions between molecules are useful in a wide range of applications but can be difficult to apply effectively. In particular, variations in cost and accuracy across different levels of theory (method and basis set combinations) makes it challenging to select an appropriate level of theory for a given chemical system. In this work, we train ∆-machine learning models to predict interaction energy errors for 81 levels of theory versus a reference and simple polynomial models to quantify computational cost for a meaningful subset of these methods. We demonstrate how a large language model (LLM) can leverage these models to select appropriate levels of theory and run computations autonomously on distributed resources, significantly reducing the barrier to obtaining accurate interaction energies.

item.title: Can Two Metals Be Chosen Independently for Electrochemical C–N Coupling?
item.description: Electrochemical C–N coupling could produce urea directly from CO or CO2 and nitrogen oxides under mild conditions. Bimetallic catalysts offer neighboring sites with different binding preferences, but choosing a suitable metal for each intermediate does not necessarily identify the most active pair. We screen 80 ordered A3B surfaces and investigate how metal selection affects reactivity at Zn3M interfaces using DFT transition-state calculations and comparative kinetic modeling. Although *CO and *N preferentially bind to different metals, both retain their metal coordination in the C–N bond-forming transition state. Changing the CO-binding metal therefore affects both CO availability and the coupling barrier. Stronger CO binding can increase coverage while making bond formation more difficult. Zn3Cu has the lowest coupling barrier, but its low CO coverage limits the rate. Zn3Pt has a higher barrier yet gives the highest predicted comparative coupling rate among the alloys studied at U = 0 V versus RHE. This comparison shows how evaluating adsorption or bond-forming kinetics alone can misidentify the preferred metal pair. Considering their combined effects provides a mechanistic basis for prioritizing Zn-based bimetallic catalysts for experimental testing.

item.title: Brewing Coffee in Ethanol Instead of Water: A Multi-Technique Pilot Study
item.description: Water extracts chlorogenic acids, which contribute to the sourness and bitterness of coffee, together with caffeine. We examined whether a less polar solvent changes that balance. Coarse-ground coffee was brewed for 20 minutes at 75 degrees Celsius in deionized water or 95 percent denatured ethanol and the extracts followed by UV-Vis and infrared spectroscopy; spent grounds from earlier brews were examined by electron and optical microscopy. The caffeine-region band near 275 nm grew about three times faster in water, while the chlorogenic acid region near 320 nm was suppressed proportionally more in ethanol, raising the ratio of the two bands from about 1.2 to 1.5 to 1.7 within a large reading uncertainty, and only the ethanol extracts showed a scattering baseline. Infrared spectra of the undiluted extracts were dominated by the solvents, identified isopropanol as the ethanol’s denaturant and showed no coffee band above the detection limit, and ethanol-brewed grounds more often showed exposed cell walls. These pilot data point to slower, partially selective extraction in ethanol, a direction relevant to lower-acid coffee concentrates, although acidity and caffeine were not measured directly. We also report the measurement problems the data revealed.

item.title: Probing the dimensionality of confinement in soft nanoreactors through plasmonic nanoparticles nucleation
item.description: Soft nanoscale confinement fundamentally alters the thermodynamic and kinetic landscape of chemical reactions, yet a predictive understanding of how nanoreactor geometry dictates reactivity remains elusive. In this work, we demonstrate that the dimensionality of soft confinement governs the onset of nanomaterial formation. By systematically tuning the water-to-surfactant molar ratio () in self-assembled lecithin reverse micelles, we decoupled the geometry of the host template from its chemical composition. We utilized the in situ nucleation of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) as an active optical and structural probe across isotropic, anisotropic, and bulk-like spatial domains. Correlating UV-Vis spectroscopy with small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) analyses, we reveal that confinement dimensionality acts as an ON/OFF switch for the reduction of gold ions. Under extreme isotropic confinement (), where the interfacial water network is severely restricted, AuNP formation is suppressed for at least 30 days. Conversely, a hydration-induced structural transition toward anisotropic, wormlike domains () coincides with the onset of AuNP nucleation and yields the highest reaction extent. Finally, further expansion into bulk-like regimes () dilutes the gold precursor within the aqueous domains, attenuating the reaction yield. We rationalize these trends within a phenomenological framework based on classical nucleation theory, highlighting confinement dimensionality as a design parameter for soft nanoreactors and tailored plasmonic nanomaterials.

item.title: Deposit optics, film thickness and acquisition date confound Raman spectra of dried droplets
item.description: Laboratory mixtures of known composition serve as ground truth for explainable AI (XAI) in vibrational spectroscopy, on the assumption that the class difference is the spectrum of the added molecule. We tested this assumption on a public Raman dataset (785 nm) of 16 dried droplets in a 2 × 2 design: a phosphatidylcholine–phenylalanine–lactate base with or without collagen–mucin and with or without DNA. Besides the 16,107 spectra, we used three records stored with the data but not analysed before: white-light images, LiveTrack focus heights and acquisition timestamps. All inference was at the droplet level. DNA raised the base bands more than any DNA band, and the two added components were not additive (p = 0.032). DNA doubled the Raman yield of the deposit (×1.97, p = 2 × 10-4). Deposit optical density in the white-light images predicted yield across droplets (r = 0.93) and within most droplets, and with optical density in the model the DNA effect fell to ×1.05 (95% CI 0.77–1.44). Focus heights agreed with a thicker film: yield rose with local height in DNA-free deposits but much less with DNA (p = 3 × 10-4). Band ratios to phenylalanine still changed with DNA after adjustment for optical density. Five maps had been acquired 8–15 days after the rest; they showed a 3.2-fold higher background, and acquisition date was predictable from held-out droplets. The DNA class therefore combines deposit optics, a modest compositional change and a date-dependent background. Attributions should be judged against this decomposed effect rather than against reference bands of DNA.

item.title: Ligand-Length Asymmetry Controls Nanoscale Heat Flow in Gold Janus Nanorods
item.description: Plasmonic nanoparticles play a crucial role in enabling technologies used in medical, catalytic, and imaging applications. Introducing particle heterogeneity in Janus nanoparticles provides a route for molecular-level control of heat transport across nanoscale length scales. Here, we show that the temperature field generated by gold Janus nanorods in water can be tuned by engineering the length of one of the ligand layers. Using non-equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate nanorods coated via self-assembly with a hydrophobic octanethiolate monolayer and a hydrophilic hydroxy-terminated alkanethiolate monolayer of varying lengths (3 to 13 carbon atoms). Increasing the hydrophilic ligand length from 3 to 13 carbon atoms,at comparable heat rates of ∼1 μW, decreases the temperature of the water adjacent to the hydrophilic domain by approximately 16 K and reduces the temperature contrast between the hydrophobic and hydrophilic regions by a factor of three, from ∼23 to ∼7 K. Simulations at constant coverage show that chain length accounts for most of this reduction by increasing ligand–water Kapitza resistance and shell thickness, whereas the lower grafting density of long-chain monolayers mainly increases gold–ligand resistance. The hydrophobic domain shows no systematic variation within the statistical uncertainty. The temperature contrast persists near the hydrophobic–hydrophilic–water three-phase boundary, indicating weak lateral heat transfer along the ligand coating. Our findings establish ligand-length asymmetry as a molecular strategy for designing materials to control anisotropic heat flow and nanoscale temperature contrast in Janus nanorods.

item.title: Emergence of Glass-like Thermal Transport through Anion-Engineering in Complex Silver Gallium Germanium Chalcogenides
item.description: Designing crystalline materials with ultralow thermal conductivity remains an important challenge for optimizing thermoelectric energy conversion and thermal barrier coatings. Crystalline solids exhibiting glass-like thermal transport are of special interest because they approach the minimum thermal conductivity achievable in an ordered structure. Here, we investigate the ultralow thermal conductivity of crystalline AgGaGeS8-8xSe8x and Ag2-xGa2-xGe2+xS8-8xSe8x (x = 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00). In these systems, selenium incorporation strongly suppresses crystalline thermal transport, leading to glass-like properties while preserving structural crystallinity. Across all compositions, the ultralow thermal conductivity is associated with a disordered silver substructure characterized by weak Ag–Ch interactions and pronounced anharmonicity, where selenium substitution promotes softening of the silver dynamics. Heat-capacity measurements reveal boson peaks in the endmember compounds, which for AgGaGe3Se8 is significantly more intense and shifted to lower temperature. Together, these results suggest that selenium promotes low-frequency silver vibrations that drive the emergence of glass-like thermal transport. Furthermore, selenium exhibits a pronounced preference for the chalcogen site most strongly interacting with silver, demonstrating that local anion chemistry, rather than average composition, governs the thermal transport response. This selective occupancy provides a structural basis for the emergence of glass-like thermal conductivity at remarkably low selenium contents.

item.title: Enzymatic Conversion from a Vicinal Diol to a Vicinal Diketone: Computational Study of the Conserved 6-Pyruvoyltetrahydropterin-Forming Stage in Mammalian and Bacterial PTPS
item.description: As a zinc- and magnesium-dependent triphosphatase, 6-pyruvoyl tetrahydropterin synthase (PTPS) catalyzes the conversion of dihydroneopterin triphosphate (H2NTP) to 6-pyruvoyltetrahydropterin (PPH4) and a triphosphate ion, representing a typical reaction for vicinal diketone biosynthesis from vicinal diol. The molecular mechanism of PTPS remains elusive owing to the lack of structural data containing native substrate H2NTP and magnesium ion. Here, we performed a quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) investigation based on a predicted PTPS structure, elucidating the complete atomistic reaction mechanism for triphosphate ion formation and stereoselective product generation. The overall catalytic reaction of PTPS proceeds via two half-reactions, each comprising four sequential proton-transfer steps. Both half-reactions involve the conversion of a hydroxyl group on the substrate into a carbonyl group, ultimately furnishing the pyruvoyl-containing product PPH4. The third proton transfer in the first half-reaction occurs preferentially on the Si-face of the critical carbanion intermediate, yielding the (R)-configured product, in agreement with the reported experimental detection results. These calculations not only unveil the structural origins of stereoselective vicinal diketone product formation, but also uncover a non-canonical triphosphate elimination pathway driven by a charge-center shift that facilitates C–O bond cleavage. These findings broaden the mechanistic paradigm of triphosphatase-mediated phosphate chemistry and offer foundational insights for synthesizing vicinal diketones from vicinal diols.

item.title: Opposite Effects of Removing Ethylene Carbonate from the Electrolyte on Ni-Rich Layered Oxide and Mn-Rich Olivine Phosphate Cathodes
item.description: Ethylene carbonate (EC)-free electrolytes are promising for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries. However, their benefits have been demonstrated primarily for layered oxide cathodes, while their effects on olivine phosphates remain unclear. Here, we show that EC removal accelerates the degradation of LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 (LMFP64), in contrast to LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811). Experiments and first-principles calculations suggest that these opposite responses reflect distinct degradation pathways associated with transition-metal–oxygen (TM–O) covalency. On NCM811, strongly hybridized O 2p states near the Fermi level favor EC dehydrogenation, initiating degradation; EC removal eliminates this pathway. In contrast, olivine models exhibit weaker TM 3d–O 2p hybridization, more ionic TM–O bonding, and stronger PF6− adsorption at TM sites. Without EC, experiments on LMFP64 reveal salt decomposition before cycling and accelerated degradation; EC otherwise limits anion access to TM sites. These findings show that the effect of EC removal is cathode-dependent and can be rationalized by TM–O covalency.

item.title: Patent Landscape of Gemini (Dimeric) Surfactants: Cationic Dominance in Intellectual Property versus the Emerging Green Surfactant Narrative
item.description: Gemini (dimeric) surfactants, molecules bearing two hydrophobic tails and two head groups joined by a spacer, have been developed across cationic, anionic, nonionic, zwitterionic, sugar-based, and amino acid-based chemistries over several decades. To the author's knowledge, this review is the first to combine a systematic patent landscape analysis spanning all major charge classes with a survey of current academic research trends to ask a direct question: Does patent activity track academic attention in this field? Drawing on 41 patent families listed in this review (Supporting Information S1) and over 20 peer-reviewed sources, the answer is no. Cationic quaternary ammonium gemini surfactants, driven mainly by enhanced oil recovery, corrosion inhibition, antimicrobial, and personal care applications, account for 25 of the 41 patent families identified here. In contrast, recent academic reviews describe amino acid- and sugar-based gemini surfactants, rather than cationic quaternary ammonium chemistry, as the field's emerging green surfactant direction; searches specifically for arginine- or lysine-specific gemini surfactant patents returned no on-point results. This review further documents a recurring definitional ambiguity between "two hydrophobic tails" and "two charge centres" in patent claim language, a near absence of true single-molecule zwitterionic gemini surfactants, and no agricultural or pesticide adjuvant application identified for any gemini surfactant charge type in either the patent or the academic searches. These findings identify several concrete, evidence-based directions for future synthetic, formulation, and intellectual property work.

item.title: Radical‑Mediated Formal Anti‑Markovnikov Hydroalkenylation of Unactivated Alkenes Enabled by a Functional Alkenyl‑Radical Surrogate Strategy
item.description: Although alkenyl radicals are conceptually desirable for anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation, their direct addition to unactivated alkenes is kinetically inaccessible owing to their intrinsically low electrophilicity and competing strong hydrogen atom abstraction reactivity. Herein, we establish a novel strategy to realize the first radical‑mediated formal anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation of unactivated alkenes. This approach utilizes the combination of highly electrophilic triphenylphosphonium methyl (TPPM) radicals with weak H atom abstraction reactivity and carbonyl compounds as practical alkenyl‑radical surrogates. The transformation begins with the photocatalytic reduction of bromomethyl triphenylphosphonium bromide to generate TPPM radicals, which add to unactivated alkenes to form carbon-centered radicals that abstract a hydrogen atom from thiophenol. The resulting phosphonium salts subsequently undergo an in‑situ Wittig reaction with carbonyl compounds to furnish the devised hydroalkenylation products. This protocol exhibits good functional group tolerance, broad substrate scope covering both activated and unactivated olefins, and allows late‑stage functionalization of natural product derivatives.

item.title: Tetrathiafulvalene-Based Molecular Qubit Frameworks with Room-Temperature Quantum Coherence
item.description: Molecular qubits, owing to their designability and tunability, have emerged as fundamental units for quantum technologies. Among them, molecular qubit frameworks (MQFs) offer unique advantages in long-range ordered lattices and microporosity that provide well-defined phonon environments and guest-tunable spin dynamics. These features greatly enhance qubit performance and enable room temperature quantum operations, holding promise for quantum sensing applications. Herein, we compare the qubit performance of 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) and tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoic acid (H4TTFTB), which form stable radicals upon spontaneous oxidation in the air. We found that optical phonons dominate spin relaxation in HHTP, whereas H4TTFTB exhibits stronger spin-orbit coupling and higher acoustic phonon population that account for its shorter spin relaxation time. Meanwhile, H4TTFTB features a nuclear-spin-free core and in turn a prolonged phase memory time, making it a favorable qubit candidate. Furthermore, we synthesized three MQFs using H4TTFTB as the ligand, which not only retain the superior room-temperature qubit performance but also possess porous channels, establishing a viable platform for future quantum information applications.

item.title: Regioselective sugar epimerization to rare sugar on ruthenium surface
item.description: Rare sugars, monosaccharides that occur only rarely in nature, exhibit physicochemical and biological properties distinct from those of naturally abundant sugars such as D-glucose. Their widespread utilization has been hindered by limitations in existing production methods, which rely primarily on equilibrium-constrained biocatalytic cascades or on synthetic approaches requiring multiple steps or organic reagents. Here we show the one-pot heterogeneous catalytic epimerization of methyl glucosides into rare sugar derivatives over supported Ru catalysts under hydrogen atmosphere in water. Among the supported metals examined, Ru uniquely promotes regioselective stereoinversion of 1-O-methyl β-D-glucopyranoside at the C3 position to produce 1-O-methyl β-D-allopyranoside without requiring additional reagents or multistep reactions. Isotopelabeling experiments reveal that dehydrogenation and hydrogenation proceed substantially faster than net epimerization, identifying surface-confined molecular rotation of a keto intermediate as the rate-determining step. Computer simulations further show that the experimentally observed regioselectivity originates from the low rotational free energy barriers and relatively high stability of the keto intermediate on the Ru surface. These findings identify molecular rotational dynamics on catalyst surfaces as a governing principle for stereochemical inversion reactions.

item.title: Revealing Phase-Controlled Surface Structure in PtNi Nanocatalysts via In-situ Gas Cell Transmission Electron Microscopy
item.description: The rational design of catalysts capable of efficiently utilizing CO2 is critical for sustainable chemical processes. The Super-dry reforming of methane (Super-DRM), which couples dry reforming of methane (DRM) with the reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reactions, offers a promising route to maximize CO2 conversion. Modulating the crystal phase of nanocatalysts offers a powerful strategy to enhance catalytic performance, yet the relationship between bulk phase and catalytic behavior remains poorly understood. A significant obstacle in resolving this issue is obtaining atomic-level insights on the surface structure of phase-controlled catalyst under reaction conditions. In this study, we employ in-situ gas cell transmission electron microscopy to investigate the surface structure of faceted PtNi nanoparticles during Super-DRM at moderate temperatures (550 ℃). Atomic-resolution in-situ observations reveal that the reaction environment induces a pronounced nickel segregation and subsequent coke formation on the surface of disordered A1-PtNi nanoparticles. In contrast, the ordered L10 phase exhibits remarkable resistance to such segregation on its {111} facets. This structural rigidity effectively suppresses coke formation and lowers the kinetic barrier for CH4 activation by 27 kJ/mol compared to the disordered phase. Complemented by in-situ spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, our findings demonstrate that the bulk crystal ordering acts as an anchor for surface structures, governing the catalytic behaviors. This study unveils a direct atomic-level link between crystal ordering, surface reconstruction, and catalytic performance, offering valuable design principles for robust intermetallic catalysts in CO2 utilization.

item.title: Electrochemically driven thermomechanical energy harvesting
A database-wide atlas of single-crystal filters for thermal neutron beams
item.description: Single-crystal filters that pass thermal neutrons and remove epithermal and fast neutrons and γ rays have been chosen from a handful of materials. For 18 449 inorganic crystals of the Materials Project, the thickness L₀.₈ at which a large single crystal oriented away from Bragg reflections transmits 80% of a 300 K Maxwellian beam over 0.5–3 Å was computed, together with its rejection −ln T of a 1/E neutron spectrum (1 eV–100 keV), of a fission spectrum and of 1 and 6 MeV photons at that thickness; 3 437 crystals have density-functional and 1 279 machine-learned phonons. A composition-only proxy reproduces the bulk order of L₀.₈ (Spearman ρ = 0.83 at 293 K, 0.95 at 77 K) but not the top of the ranking, which a single elastic Debye temperature largely recovers. Against measured total cross-sections the acceptance criterion fixed in advance was not met (6 of 13 crystals fail); restricted to single-crystal data, 4 of 11 fail, or 6 of 11 without an allowance for the spread between datasets; and the model lies above all four sapphire datasets. With a model uncertainty of 0.138 in ln L₀.₈ propagated by 20 000 Monte Carlo draws, the Pareto front of commercially grown crystals (epithermal against 1 MeV photon rejection) consists of known filters alone with probability 0.10 at 293 K and 0.04 at 77 K, and cooling reorders it. No grown crystal that is not a known filter beats sapphire with probability above 0.90, the level fixed for a statement. 6H-SiC and chrysoberyl are candidates on the epithermal axis: the probability that 6H-SiC rejects the 1/E spectrum better than sapphire is 0.85 at 293 K and 0.88 at 77 K (chrysoberyl: 0.66 and 0.85); with an error component shared by all compounds it rises to 0.93 and 0.95, and with sapphire corrected by its measured residual it falls to 0.69 and 0.73. On the fission spectrum neither candidate is distinguishable from sapphire. Counting every transmitted particle instead of the uncollided ones changes the epithermal rejection by −0.23 to −6.28 and reorders the front, so uncollided figures of merit rank filters optimistically for uncollimated beams. The pipeline that produces the atlas is openly available; the atlas and its uncertainties will be archived openly on acceptance.

item.title: Diastereoselective Synthesis of Hetero-[2]-Ladderanes
item.description: Conformationally rigid heterobicyclic motifs with well-defined exit vectors have emerged as valuable isosteric replacements for pyridine. While these rigid 3D structures successfully mimic 3,5-disubstituted pyridine derivatives, no isosteric analogues of 2,3-disubstituted pyridines have been reported, despite their widespread occurrence in bioactive compounds. Herein, we report the first diastereoselective synthesis of hetero-[2]-ladderanes, representing a new class of potential 2,3-disubstituted pyridine isosteres, via carbonyl photoexcitation. This protocol is amenable to a variety of 2-azetines and isatins, with remarkable functional-group tolerance, enabling rapid construction of complex spiro-oxa-aza-[2]-ladderanes as single diastereomers. Notably, benzaldehyde derivatives could also participate, affording oxa-aza-[2]-ladderanes with high stereoselectivity. Exit-vector analysis of an oxa-aza-[2]ladderane and a 2,3-disubstituted pyridine-based drug demonstrated the potential of this scaffold as a possible isosteric mimic of 2,3-disubstituted pyridine. Experimental-based mechanistic studies combined with density functional theory have rationalized the observed reactivity and selectivity. Finally, we explored an unprecedented strainenabled, aromaticity-driven Grob-type fragmentation of a hetero-[2]-ladderane, yielding synthetically valuable αhydroxy-β-amino ketone and aminotriol derivatives.

item.title: Non-structural proteins 2 (nsP2) in Alphavirus: a useful target for drug discovery studies
item.description: The Alphavirus genus consists of single-stranded positive-sense ribonucleic acid (RNA) viruses belonging to the Togaviridae family. They are considered arthropod-borne viruses (arboviruses) and the medically most important are: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), Sindbis virus (SINV), and the three American equine encephalitis viruses, i.e., the Eastern equine encephalitis virus (EEEV), Western equine encephalitis virus (WEEV), and Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV). There is currently no approved direct-acting antiviral for the treatment of these diseases. As part of our antiviral drug discovery program focused on Alphaviruses and the non-structural protein 2 (nsP2). We employed diverse in silico methods, ranging from static scanning to temporal pocket evaluation, to assess the druggability of the alphaviral nsP2. Our results suggested that cryptic sites could be better explored for drug discovery campaigns, as current efforts have focused only on the nsP2 active site.

item.title: Direct Access to α-Aryl-β-Amino Aldehydes via Hypervalent Iodine-Mediated Oxidative Rearrangement of Cinnamyl Amines
item.description: Selective synthesis of α-aryl-β-amino aldehydes remains less developed despite considerable progress in Mannich reactions, aza-Michael additions and asymmetric hydroformylation. Here we report a phenyliodine(III) bis(trifluoroacetate) (PIFA)-mediated oxidative rearrangement of cinnamyl amines through formal 1,2-aryl migration. The reaction proceeds at 0 °C under ambient air and accommodates diverse nitrogen substituents, migrating aryl groups and pharmaceutical-derived substrates. A 6-gram preparation and subsequent transformations to β-amino acids, 1,3-amino alcohols, 1,3-diamines and azetidines, together with the synthesis of a valifenalate isomer, demonstrate the synthetic utility of the aldehyde products. Mechanistic experiments suggest a pathway involving a bis(trifluoroacetate) intermediate. An initial asymmetric variant using chiral iodine(III) reagents furnished a celecoxib-derived chiral aldehyde, with up to 77% ee measured for its reduced chiral alcohol derivative.

item.title: Machine learning–driven inverse design of nanofiltration membranes for selective Mg2+/Na+ separation
item.description: Desalination brine, a byproduct of seawater desalination, contains valuable resources, including magnesium. Recovering magnesium requires selectively retaining Mg2+ while allowing the dominant monovalent cation, Na+, to permeate. Nanofiltration (NF) membranes fabricated by interfacial polymerization are promising for this Mg2+/Na+ separation, but their performance depends on coupled formulation and processing variables that are inefficient to optimize through trial and error. Here, we demonstrate a workflow integrating dataset curation, forward prediction, and inverse design of thin-film composite NF membranes. A dataset of 1,253 entries, comprising literature and in-house records, was cleaned, imputed, and augmented through chemically constrained permutation of interchangeable polymer, solvent, and salt variables in the training split only. Optimized extremely randomized tree regressors predicted pure water permeability, solute rejection, and intermediate membrane properties, achieving test-set coefficients of determination above 0.79. Shapley analysis indicated that permeability was governed primarily by formulation and processing variables, whereas rejection depended mainly on solute identity and charge, as well as membrane tightness. Using Bayesian optimization with a scalarized objective, two membrane recipes with favorable Mg2+/Na+ selectivity were identified and experimentally validated. The inversely designed membranes exhibited the required Mg2+/Na+ selectivity, demonstrating the capability of this workflow to design Mg2+-selective NF membranes for resource recovery from desalination brine.

item.title: Schizotrins B-E from the Cultured Cyanobacterium CCIBt3280 - Unique Biosynthetic Signatures and Evidence for an Antibacterial Target
item.description: We report the discovery and chemical structures of schizotrins B-E (1-4) isolated from cultures of Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280. These peptides were identified by spectroscopic and spectrometric analyses. Their absolute configuration was established by Marfey’s and advanced NMR analysis, computational modeling, and Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280 genome analysis. Conserved A- and B-type ketoreductase motifs revealed a stereochemical control of αketoreduction in polyketide natural products. Phylogenomic analyses placed Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280 within the Floridanema family-level clade, indicating that its current assignment to Phormidium should be reassessed. Genome mining uncovered numerous previously unknown schizotrin-like biosynthetic gene clusters in publicly available genomes. The antibacterial activity of peptides 1-4 were also investigated. Schizotrin B inhibited the growth of Bacillus anthracis Sterne at 1 µM. Whole-genome sequencing of spontaneous resistant mutants of B. anthracis revealed a loss-of-function mutation in psd (phosphatidylserine decarboxylase), implicating membrane phospholipid homeostasis in schizotrin B activity. Our results expanded the chemical diversity of the schizotrin family, provided new insights into the biosynthesis of αcarbonyl-containing amino acids, supported the placement of the schizotrin-producing lineage within a potentially novel cyanobacterial genus, and provided insights into the potential mechanism of schizotrins antibacterial resistance.

item.title: Identification and Experimental Validation of Repurposable Drugs Targeting the Essential ClpP1 Protease of Mycobacterium tuberculosis
item.description: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health challenge, necessitating the identification of novel therapeutic targets and accelerated drug discovery strategies. The caseinolytic protease (ClpP) complex of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) is essential for proteostasis, stress adaptation, and bacterial survival, making it an attractive yet underexplored drug target. Comparative structural analysis also revealed significant differences between mycobacterial and human ClpP S1 pockets, suggesting opportunities for selective inhibition. In this study, a structure-based drug repurposing approach was employed to identify approved drugs targeting the S1 pocket of the ClpP1 subunit, a key regulatory site involved in proteolytic activation. Virtual screening of the approved drug library against the ClpP1 crystal structure (PDB ID: 4U0G) identified Saquinavir and Raltegravir as the most promising candidates, exhibiting binding affinities of –9.1 and –9.5 kcal/mol, respectively, and favorable interactions with critical S1 pocket residues. Molecular dynamics simulations over 200 ns confirmed stable ligand binding and persistent occupancy within the S1 pocket. In vitro evaluation against M. tuberculosis H37Ra demonstrated potent concentration-dependent antimycobacterial activity, with Saquinavir showing superior efficacy (IC50 = 0.01 ± 0.007 μM; MIC = 64 μM) compared with Raltegravir (IC50 = 0.1 ± 0.09 μM; MIC ≥ 128 μM). Growth kinetics, REMA, and statistical analyses further validated their inhibitory activity. These findings validate Saquinavir and Raltegravir as potential repurposable anti-tubercular agents for further mechanistic and preclinical evaluation.

item.title: Constraint-guided equal-strut growth generates a tunable family of DNA-realizable wireframe filaments
item.description: Wireframe DNA nanostructures are built from edges of prescribed length meeting at vertices of prescribed valency, which makes their design space a geometric one: which equal-edge frameworks can be built at all, given a maximum vertex degree, a minimum edge angle and a steric clearance. We apply a constrained growth construction—each new vertex placed by trilateration at a fixed strut length from at least three placed vertices, accepted only if the resulting framework still satisfies the design constraints—and report three results. First, under a degree cap of six the construction is extremely selective: of all periodic face-choice patterns tested, only the Boerdijk–Coxeter tetrahelix grows without stalling, and it does so because its interior vertices have degree exactly six, saturating the budget. Second, raising the cap to seven unlocks a one-parameter family of kinked variants indexed by the defect spacing k, whose radius is programmable from 0.52 to 1.13 strut lengths and whose handedness alternates with k, while straightness stays above 0.99. Values k ∈ {3, 5, 8} stall for an identifiable reason—the capped vertex lands at unit distance from a fourth earlier vertex—and run freely at a cap of eight. Both caps are within demonstrated multi-arm junction capability. Third, two members of the family, the pure tetrahelix and a k = 6 variant, were routed into DNA, energy-minimised and run for 5×105 oxDNA steps at 30◦C: both are stable, with second-half mean energies −1.4919±0.0017 and −1.5004 ± 0.0019 per nucleotide and shape changes under 4%. The kinked variant routes into 8 strand cycles against the tetrahelix’s 22. We also report what did not survive checking: a twist–stretch coupling that vanished under length convergence, and a circular-dichroism sign rule that its own descriptor failed to predict.

item.title: Exciton Diffusion Drives Efficiency Roll-off in TADF OLEDs
item.description: 2 Abstract Despite their potential to deliver high-efficiency organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), those using thermally activated delayed fluorescent (TADF) emitters often suffer from a large drop in efficiency at high luminance. This effect is known as efficiency roll-off and is a longstanding issue for these devices, which has limited their commercial deployment. We have discovered that the degree of overlap between the photoluminescence (PL) and absorption spectra drives singlet exciton diffusion and is a strong predictor of the magnitude of efficiency roll-off in TADF OLEDs. This effect is especially important in OLEDs made with multiresonant (MR)-TADF materials given their intense low-energy short-range charge transfer absorption bands. MR-TADF OLEDs are very appealing due to their narrow emission spectra; however, their small Stokes shift leads to large spectral overlap and contributes to these devices showing severe efficiency roll-off. Developing TADF materials that have a larger Stokes shift whilst maintaining their bright, narrow emission would help minimize efficiency roll-off while securing high internal quantum efficiencies, features particularly relevant for displays.

item.title: Polarization Is Required to Model Electrostatic Preorganization: The Case of Chorismate Mutase
Uniform Gel Networks with Amide-Rich Crosslinking Domains Amplify Weak Interactions for Growth of Ultrasmall Nanoparticles without Added Strong Ligand
item.description: Synthesizing ultrasmall thermoresponsive nanoparticles within poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPA) hydrogels without the use of strong ligands remains challenging, as intrinsically weak interfacial interactions and structural heterogeneity in conventional networks often lead to poor size control and aggregation. Here, we report a programmable PNIPA-based hydrogel constructed from star-shaped polymers via living radical polymerization, in which a homogeneous network containing locally reinforced crosslinking domains enables ligand-free in situ formation of ultrasmall metal nanoparticles. The uniform network provides a spatially consistent reaction environment, allowing synchronized and controllable particle growth across length scales. Nanoparticle size is governed by network architecture rather than by synthetic conditions, and the resulting hydrogel composites exhibit exceptional stability under thermal cycling and harsh chemical environments, despite relying solely on amide functionalities. Stabilization does not arise from rigid immobilization or strong ligand coordination along the polymer chains; instead, it emerges from the collective engagement of multiple spatially distributed, amide-enriched crosslinking domains. These reinforced domains generate a cooperative multiple-anchoring effect, creating a soft yet adaptive chelation-like confinement. This work establishes a versatile platform for strong-ligand-free yet robust and controllable nanoparticle synthesis, extendable to colloidal dispersions, diverse polymer matrices, and various metal nanoparticles.

item.title: A dual-targeting nitrogen mustard-class I HDAC inhibitor hybrid molecule is superior to the combination of an HDAC inhibitor plus chlorambucil in glioblastoma cells
Polarization-Driven Hydride Transfer Promotes Cobalt Tetrasulfophthalocyanine-Catalyzed Hydrogen Evolution by Five Orders of Magnitude
item.description: The hydricity of M–H intermediates is a key descriptor and optimization target for the rational design of molecular hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts. Adsorption to an electrode surface is known to augment catalytic rate, but it remains unclear how adsorption affects M-H hydricity. Herein, we quantitatively compare the catalytic activity and mechanism of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) from cobalt tetrasulfophthalocyanine (CoTSPc) in a dissolved aqueous form (CoTSPc(aq)) and when adsorbed to the surface of a carbon electrode (CoTSPc/C). At the same electrode potential, CoTSPc/C catalyzes HER at a rate that is over five orders of magnitude faster than CoTSPc(aq). Mechanistic studies indicate that both CoTSPc/C and CoTSPc(aq) catalyze HER via a rate-limiting hydride transfer to a proton donor in solution to form H2. Hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc(aq) is a purely chemical step defined by a constant hydricity of 22.4 kcal mol−1 that is independent of applied potential. In contrast, hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc/C is strongly polarization dependent, decreasing hydricity by ~23 kcal mol−1 V−1 to values as low as 1.2 kcal mol−1 at −1.1 V vs SHE, leading to the observed rate promotion. We attribute this mechanistic change to the positioning of the CoTSPc-H intermediate within the electrochemical double layer, such that the hydride traverses the interfacial electrostatic potential difference during the RLS. These results demonstrate the power of surface adsorption to generate highly reactive molecular hydrides and fundamentally reshape the free energy landscape of electrocatalysis.

item.title: A bipartite quantum-acoustic architecture stabilizes multi-exciton solitons at 323 K
item.description: A fundamental thermal paradox has constrained the physical viability of quantum coherent Davydov solitons in quasi-one-dimensional (1D) peptide helices for over 50 years. At 323 K (0.0278 eV), ambient thermal noise disrupts the localized amide I self-trapping resonance, rapidly scattering multi-quanta excitations into delocalized thermal states on femtosecond timescales. Here, a non-equilibrium, bipartite quantum-acoustic stabilization architecture resolves this long-standing decoherence veto via a two-scale viscoelastic coacervate boundary that opens a terahertz transverse acoustic pinning gap, extending three-exciton coherence half-lives from 6.5 fs to 42.6 fs—a pre-thermalization window sufficient to outpace non-radiative intramolecular vibrational energy redistribution (IVR) prior to classical mechanical stepping. By examining the continuous α-helices of eukaryotic F/V-type rotary ATPase c-rings as an evolutionary proof-of-concept archetype and directly simulating both biological α-helical and synthetic 3₁₀-helical manifolds in a 136 × 136 three-exciton open quantum system master equation, we demonstrate that a cooperative, reaction-field-polarized variable-dipole linactant (6.0 D) induces a 0.058 eV single-quantum vibrational Stark–polaron trap (2.1 kBT ) and a > 0.25 eV cooperative three-exciton well. Incorporating exact nearest-neighbor Lang–Firsov polaron coupling alongside three-body single-bond Morse/Pauli over-compression repulsion stabilizes the dipole-active |2₁₅,1₁₆⟩ ± |1₁₅,2₁₆⟩ charge-shared ground doublet 57 meV below the super-dephasing |3,0⟩ manifold, locking the soliton core onto the central defect dimer with 88% spatial localization fidelity. Finally, we map each term of the bipartite Hamiltonian directly onto an orthogonal click and fluoride-exchange (CuAAC/SuFEx/GeFEx-S/PFEx) synthetic blueprint to establish a falsifiable, room-temperature quantum-acoustic metamaterial.

item.title: Acetylcholinesterase Activity Modulation by Proteinogenic Amino Acid Ester Ferulates salts with Enhanced Solubility and Antioxidant Properties
item.description: Ferulic acid (FA) is a phenolic antioxidant whose potential applications are limited by poor aqueous solubility and bioavailability. Novel ferulate salts of ethyl, propyl, and isopropyl esters of L-tyrosine and L-phenylalanine were synthesized and characterized in terms of their physicochemical properties, antioxidant activity, and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibition. All synthesized ferulates exhibited improved aqueous solubility compared with FA, with tyrosine ethyl ester ferulate, [TyrOEt][FA], showing the highest solubility. The salts retained or enhanced antioxidant activity, with tyrosine-derived compounds exhibiting nearly twofold higher activity than FA in the ORAC assay. The ferulate salts also demonstrated stronger AChE inhibition than FA, with phenylalanine isopropyl ester ferulate, [PheOiPr][FA], showing the greatest inhibitory potency among the ferulates. Comparison with the corresponding chloride salts indicated that the amino acid ester cations were primarily responsible for AChE inhibition. Kinetic analysis revealed a mixed inhibition mechanism with a predominant competitive component for the most active compounds. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations identified interactions with key aromatic residues within the AChE binding gorge, while MM/GBSA calculations supported favorable binding of the amino acid esters. The synthesized compounds generally had limited effects on L929 fibroblast viability, although tyrosine propyl ester salts showed greater cytotoxicity. These findings demonstrate that salt formation with amino acid esters improves the physicochemical properties of FA while preserving its antioxidant potential, whereas AChE inhibitory activity is primarily determined by the structure of the amino acid ester moiety and its interactions with key residues within the enzyme's active-site gorge.

item.title: Joule Heating Induced Structural Evolution of Ordered Mesoporous Mg-Al Spinel-Related Oxides
item.description: Coupling block copolymer self-assembly with ultrafast Joule heating enables second-scale crystallization of ordered mesoporous oxides while preserving long-range mesoscopic order. Using this strategy, we synthesize long-range ordered mesoporous magnesium-aluminum oxide frameworks at low magnesium contents exhibiting defect spinel-related nanocrystalline structures. Ex situ isothermal holds at 1000 to 1155 °C reveal rapid crystallite enlargement followed by a plateau in apparent crystallite size. In pure γ-alumina, this early saturation, together with retention of the ordered mesostructure, is consistent with geometrically constrained crystallite growth. Magnesium incorporation enables further crystallite enlargement before saturation, yielding larger defect-spinel-related domains while retaining long-range mesoscopic order. We further demonstrate the incorporation of in situ crystallized platinum nanoparticles within the ordered magnesium-aluminum oxide framework and their activity for methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation at 350 °C. These results demonstrate that ultrafast Joule heating can access distinct crystallization trajectories in compositionally modified mesoporous oxides that are precluded by mesostructural collapse during conventional furnace heating.

item.title: Electron Density of Delocalized Bonds from Correlated One-Particle Density Matrices
item.description: Extending bond-delocalization analysis to correlated one-particle density matrices requires separating fractional occupations from the projector structure underlying determinant-based algorithms. We define the electron density of delocalized bonds (EDDB) by combining bond-orbital projection (BOP) results for cumulative spectral projectors with occupation-gap weights. A structural bound on the raw BOP matrix ensures a positive semidefinite density layer bounded by its parent density. The construction recovers determinant limits, provides consistent spin conventions under stated conditions, and uses an orbital-pair population matrix consistent with the parent orbital populations. An analytic three-center model distinguishes this construction from direct substitution of a fractionaloccupation density into BOP. We further distinguish full-space spectral resolution from subsequent working-space reduction, and numerical occupation grouping and representability preprocessing from the exact definition. The resulting formulation extends EDDB analysis beyond single determinants while making its mathematical properties and limitations explicit. The proposed method is fully implemented in the latest release of runEDDB.

item.title: Synthesis of N-Protected L-DOPA(acetonide) Derivatives
item.description: The modular synthesis of N-protected L-DOPA(acetonide) derivatives from readily available H-L-DOPA-OH is reported. A consecutive protecting group strategy and a partial hydrogenolytic removal affords H-L-DOPA(acetonide)-OH as key intermediate. Subsequent N-protection provides Fmoc-, Boc-, Cbz-, and Alloc-protected derivatives in excellent yields (95–99%). The key intermediate was further converted into the corresponding N-carboxyanhydride – a building block for polypeptide synthesis.

item.title: Nanoscale Phase Engineering and Magnetic Property Enhancement in High-Entropy Alloy Nanoparticles by Continuous Microparticle Laser Fragmentation in Liquid
item.description: High-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) offer compositional and structural tunability for applications, like water splitting, H2O2 production, or magnetocaloric technologies. Therefore, the interplay between composition, structure, and functionality is of significant interest for materials´ functionality optimization. Microparticle laser fragmentation in liquid flow (MP-LFL) is an emerging scalable method for nanoalloy production, but remains underexplored for HEA NPs. Here, we investigate CrFeCoNiX (X = Ga, Cu, Mo) HEA NPs fabricated by MP-LFL in ethanol and examine how compositional variations affect elemental homogeneity, size, phase structure, and magnetic properties. Microscopy, diffraction, size analysis, and magnetometry reveal particle sizes of 6-7 nm and pronounced differences in phase structures, ranging from single-phase fcc and biphasic fcc/bcc to amorphous structures, partially contrasting the initial feedstock microparticle structures. The low saturation magnetization (Ms) of the as-synthesized superparamagnetic NPs increases strongly after in situ annealing by approximately 4-, 3-, or 24-fold for Ga-, Cu-, and Mo-containing NPs, respectively, coinciding with structural and elemental rearrangements. In contrast, the feedstock microparticles show no comparable increase, highlighting the role of the initial phase constitution in determining magnetic properties. Moreover, MP-LFL enables production of ~0.4 g/h, with a record picosecond MP-LFL mass yield of ~60%, leaving room for further optimization and high throughput.

item.title: COSMO-RS screening and experimental solid-liquid equilibrium validation of eutectic solvent candidates for CO2 capture
item.description: A combined computational -experimental strategy was applied to accelerate the identification of deep eutectic solvent (DES) candidates for CO2 capture applications. A diverse group of hydrogen bond acceptors (HBA) and hydrogen bond donors (HBD) was selected and screened as potential DES constituents. Subsequently COSMO-RS was used to predict solid-liquid equilibrium (SLE) phase behavior and CO2 infinite dilution activity coefficients. Based on this screening, selected mixtures were experimentally investigated using differential scanning calorimetry and visual observation of SLE measurements. The experimental results confirmed the formation of stable liquid phases for several systems, including Bet:TEA. In contrast, the Bet:MEA system, predicted to be liquid at ambient conditions, did not form a stable liquid phase experimentally and showed signs of decomposition. For L-tryptophan:MEA, an offset of approximately 2 K between predicted and experimental liquidus temperatures was observed, which is below the experimental uncertainty of 3 K. These findings demonstrate that COSMO-RS is an effective screening tool for identifying promising DES candidates, significantly reducing experimental effort, while highlighting the necessity of experimental validation to account for unexpected effects such as decomposition and metastable behavior. This iterative workflow can offer a time-efficient route for identifying solvents with favorable melting behavior over a broad temperature range and facilitates the development of organic-based DESs for CO2 capture applications.

item.title: Enantioselective Total Syntheses of Bousigonine A and Bisleuconothine B
item.description: Herein, we report the first enantioselective total syntheses of bousigonine A and bisleuconothine B, two heterodimeric monoterpenoid indole alkaloids. The requisite quebrachamine-type and aspidosperma-type alkaloid units were prepared divergently from a common intermediate and subsequently coupled with an eburnan-type alkaloid through bioinspired coupling reactions. The benzyl protecting group on the nitrogen played a crucial role in controlling the regioselectivity of these reactions, enabling selective bond formation at C10. Subsequent chemoselective oxidations of the coupling products furnished the characteristic quinone and N,O-acetal moieties, completing the total syntheses of both natural products. Furthermore, these synthetic studies led to a revision of the absolute configuration of bousigonine A.

item.title: Biosynthesis of acyl-CoA thioesters from simple amines, alcohols and esters enabled by co-immobilized multi-enzyme systems
item.description: Acyl-Coenzyme A derivatives are a valuable family of metabolic intermediates with many applications, such as building blocks on biosynthetic routes, protein labeling, or potential therapeutics. However, their synthesis is limited to highly activated molecules (i.e. anhydrides) or carboxylic acids. In this work, we developed two multifunctional heterogeneous biocatalysts, capable of synthesizing acyl-CoA thioesters from primary alcohols or amines using free Coenzyme A via two different stepwise enzymatic cascades. The first enzymatic cascade involves an alcohol and CoA-acylating decarboxylase that catalyzes the oxidative thioesterification of primary alcohols through consecutive oxidation of alcohols to thioesters. In the second cascade, a transaminase enables the deamination of primary amines to aldehydes, which are concurrently oxidized to acyl-CoAs by a CoA-acylating dehydrogenase, using pyruvate as the amine acceptor. In both cases, the redox cofactor (NAD+) regeneration is carried out with a water-forming NADH oxidase that thermodynamically drives the reaction. Both systems exhibited broad substrate scopes, accepting a variety of aliphatic and aromatic primary amines and alcohols. Through rational co-immobilization designs coupled to post-immobilization steps using glutaraldehyde, we achieved highly active and operationally stable multifunctional heterogeneous biocatalysts. Specifically, the system to transform propyl amine into propyl-CoA exhibited excellent performance over five consecutive reaction cycles. Finally, the oxidative thioesterification cascade was successfully coupled with the immobilized promiscuous lipase Novozyme 435, allowing the hydrolysis of the one-pot transformation of alkyl esters into acyl-CoA thioesters. These findings broaden the range of non-activated substrates for acyl-CoA biosynthesis beyond conventional carboxylic acids and create new opportunities for integrating these biocatalysts into CoA-dependent biosynthetic pathways relevant to chemical biomanufacturing and synthetic biology.

item.title: Negative effects of oxygen and halogen species on charge extraction in perovskite solar cells with fullerene electron transport layers
item.description: In this work, we explore the effect of small molecular species such as air, iodide, iodine, and triiodide species on the charge transport behavior of fullerene electron transport layers and the concomitant effects on performance and stability of perovskite solar cells. First, we show that without SnOx buffer layers, two-step vapor deposited perovskites have notable losses upon air exposure while spin-coated perovskites have minor losses. We hypothesize that these effects are caused by intrinsic organohalide excess in the CSS perovskite film, leading to an enrichment of mobile halide species such as iodide, iodine, and polyiodides, coupled with a deterioration of C60 charge transport properties. We show that the fill factor losses found in two-step vapor-deposited devices upon air exposure can be induced in spin-coated perovskites by treating their surface with potassium triiodide solutions, further implicating polyhalide species in these losses. Drift-diffusion simulations support the hypothesis that this may be explained by deep electron traps in the C60 formed by polyhalides, while O2 may form shallower traps that have more minor effects on device performance in isolation. Critically, we identify that common ammonium halide surface passivation treatments can lead to performance losses with similar current-voltage signatures during operation in time periods as short as 30 minutes. This may be caused by in situ iodine and polyhalide generation from photolysis of residual lead iodide reducing charge extraction in these solar cells. This work has important implications for the design of stable perovskite solar cells with fullerene charge transport layers.

item.title: Systematic Evaluation of Halogen Substitution in ortho-Benzoxy Phenylboronic Acid Catalysts for Amidation Reactions
item.description: Boronic acids have emerged as powerful catalysts for amidation reactions. Based on a previously identified orthobenzoxy phenylboronic acid motif, a systematic structure-activity study was performed.
